name: tcell-exhaustion
title: T-cell exhaustion vs. starting PD1+ fraction
question:
Does the exhausted (PD1+) T-cell fraction over time depend on the fraction of T cells
seeded as exhausted, and is that dependence robust across seeds?

study_card.goal: Show the robust, T-cell-intrinsic exhaustion dynamic that underlies the paper's efficacy-vs-exhaustion story.
study_card.mechanism: PD1- T cells exhaust to PD1+ after repeated TCR-engagement/refractory cycles; PD1+ cells also die faster next to PDL1+ tumors. Seeding more PD1+ cells raises the exhausted fraction.
study_card.expected_result: The end PD1+ fraction is much higher when 75% (vs 25%) of T cells start exhausted, in every seed.
study_card.main_expert_question: Do the refractory-cycle and death-rate parameters give the right exhaustion timescale vs. the paper's 3-day runs?

biological_summary:
In the paper (Hickey, Agmon et al., Cell Systems 2024, Figure 3H), repeated TCR stimulation
drives therapeutic T cells from the active PD1- state into the exhausted PD1+ state over the
course of treatment, which lowers their cytokine (IFNg) secretion and cell division — the
mechanistic reason the starting phenotype matters. The starting fraction (set ex-vivo: 25%
PD1+ with 2HC memory-skewing vs 75% PD1+ without) therefore shapes how much conversion and
killing the T cells can drive. This study isolates that dynamic: T cells seeded around a
tumor mass were followed for ~10 h across 6 seeds. When 75% of T cells started exhausted, the
exhausted fraction ended near 63% (± 22); when only 25% started exhausted it ended near 16%
(± 11) — the ordering held in all 6 seeds, a robust cell-intrinsic dynamic. (Net tumor-count
suppression, by contrast, needs larger scale — see efficacy-at-scale.)

expected_behavior.name: exhaustion_tracks_starting_fraction
expected_behavior.en: The exhausted (PD1+) T-cell fraction is higher with a 75% PD1+ start than a 25% PD1+ start.

measure.of: final PD1+ T-cell fraction, mean over 6 seeds, per starting condition

behavior_tests.name: exhaustion_tracks_starting_fraction

measure.of: final PD1+ T-cell fraction (25% start vs 75% start), 6 seeds

behavior_tests.result: PASS: 75% start ~63±22% vs 25% start ~16±11% end PD1+ (6/6 seeds)

report.title: T-cell exhaustion vs. starting PD1+ fraction
report.objective: Demonstrate the robust exhaustion dependence on the starting PD1+ fraction.
report.conclusion:
Across 6 seeds the exhausted (PD1+) T-cell fraction is far higher when more T cells start
exhausted — a clean, replicated reproduction of the paper's T-cell exhaustion dynamic.
report.caveat:
This is the T-cell-intrinsic half of the efficacy story. The population consequence
(lower tumor suppression when more T cells are exhausted) is not separable from growth
noise at this reduced scale and needs paper-scale runs.

readouts: PD1+ T-cell fraction over time (25% vs 75% start), mean ± std
